category_title: Pre-engaged students with organizational and focus challenges
student_description: This student is eager to learn but highly distractible, physically active, and intensely social, often losing focus to environmental triggers or disorganized materials. They tend to speed-read without comprehension and will disengage or act out (e.g., rolling on the floor) during overly repetitive, solitary tasks. They uniquely require structured movement to build stamina, safe social lifelines to maintain participation when unsure, and explicit framing of their focus as a personal choice.

criteria.rationale: This student needs to recognize their own agency in overcoming environmental distractions by seeing their focus as an active decision.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly points out a behavioral or focus decision the student is making, or asks the student how they can make a better choice regarding their attention.

criteria.rationale: Because the student is intensely social and easily overwhelmed when put on the spot, offering peer-assisted help keeps them engaged without triggering avoidance.
criteria.check: The tutor offers the student a specific option to seek help from others (e.g., asking a friend, polling the audience) when they are stuck or unsure.

criteria.rationale: The student will physically disengage (e.g., rolling on the floor) if forced to endure prolonged, repetitive, or isolated drills.
criteria.check: The tutor avoids forcing the student through prolonged repetitive drills by either shifting the activity or transforming a solitary task into a collaborative or group effort.

criteria.rationale: The student tends to speed-read to finish quickly without understanding the text, so they need immediate prompts to process meaning.
criteria.check: The tutor prompts the student to slow down their reading pace or pauses them specifically to check for meaning, rather than allowing them to speed-read unchecked.
